items.title: BI 249 Michael Cole: Brain Flows are the Units of Cognition
items.summary: Support the show to get full episodes, full archive, and join the Discord community.The Transmitter is an online publication that aims to deliver useful information, insights and tools to build bridges across neuroscience and advance research. Visit thetransmitter.org to explore the latest neuroscience news and perspectives, written by journalists and scientists.Read more about our partnership.Sign up for Brain Inspired email alerts to be notified every time a new Brain Inspired episode is released.To explore more neuroscience news and perspectives, visit thetransmitter.org.Michael Cole is a professor at the Center for Molecular and Behavioral Neuroscience at Rutgers University. After 10 years running The Cole Neurocognition Lab, and reflecting on the work they've done and the field more broadly, he decided to write a book: Brain Flows: How Network Dynamics Compose the Human Mind. In the book, Michael argues that brain flows are the fundamental units of brain function and therefore cognition. We discuss what a brain flow is and is not, and how viewing cognition through the brain flow lens differs from other approaches, like viewing populations of neuron activity as fundamental units of cognition. In fact, Michael has found that most of the signal processing going on is between areas of networks, not within the areas of the networks. The first part of the discussion covers those kinds of basics, then we move on to discuss how different organizational features of brain flows, like compositional hierarchies, might explain "higher" cognitive functions like value-based goals, emotion, creativity, consciousness, intelligence, and mental disorders.The Cole Neurocognition LabTwitter: @mwcole.bsky.social; @TheColeLabBook:Brain Flows: How Network Dynamics Compose the Human Mind0:00 - Intro4:43 - Brain Flows15:09 - Flow as a fundamental unit16:45 - Functional connectivity20:24 - Backstory24:31 - Activity flow modeling37:30 - Generative understanding44:12 - Hierarchical compositionality48:09 - Novelty50:50 - Cognitive control56:38 - Creativity1:14:06 - Mental health and flows1:21:51 - Consciousness and flow fields1:31:12 - AI and brain flows
